generator.program.note: The genus's own program, on the cactus base: chains of flat joints whose margins are toothed.

traits.note: Britton and Rose, The Cactaceae vol. 4 (1923), pp. 177-178, as Zygocactus (read at the Internet Archive, cactaceaedescri04brit, 2026-10-19): Zygocactus: Stems dichotomously much branched, flattened, divided into short joints; flowers terminal, polychromic, irregular; ovary terete, smooth, gradually broadening from base, bearing minute scales at top; flower-tube abruptly bent just above the ovary, ending in a serrate mouth, bearing petaloid spreading scales scattered along its sides; stamens slender, white, arranged in 2 clusters; style purple, slender, as long as stamens; stigma-lobes linear, purple, erect; fruit purple, turgid, not at all angled. Flattened short joints, so flat joints without ribs or tubercles; flowers terminal ('irregular' is left unstated: the flower code draws a spiral perianth regular, so the family's usual actinomorphic stands until it can); the ovary smooth but for minute scales, so naked; spines none (the areoles carry wool and bristles only). The reflexed perianth from the type species, as Britton and Rose treat the genus as one species.
